original_title: I enjoyed this video of Oblivion Remastered actor Wes Johnson goofing around in a sound booth dressed as Sheogorath, but a patch for the PC version would be nice too, Bethesda
summary_en: A delightful new promotional video for the Nintendo Switch 2 version of Oblivion Remastered features veteran voice actor Wes Johnson reprising his iconic role as Sheogorath. Fans are thrilled to see Johnson back in action, though some technical concerns linger.
ai_analysis: This piece highlights the enduring appeal of classic Elder Scrolls characters and voice actors, even as players grapple with the technical realities of modern remasters.

en.title: Wes Johnson Returns as Sheogorath for Oblivion Remastered Promo
en.summary: A delightful new promotional video for the Nintendo Switch 2 version of Oblivion Remastered features veteran voice actor Wes Johnson reprising his iconic role as Sheogorath. Fans are thrilled to see Johnson back in action, though some technical concerns linger.
en.body:
The eccentric Prince of Madness is back, and this time he’s bringing his signature brand of delightful chaos to a promotional video for **Oblivion Remastered**'s upcoming Nintendo Switch 2 release. Veteran **Elder Scrolls** voice actor **Wes Johnson**, the man behind countless memorable characters including Oblivion's default Imperial males and, of course, the inimitable **Sheogorath**, has returned to the sound booth. The result is a charming, behind-the-scenes glimpse that’s far more entertaining than your typical game trailer.

The video captures **Johnson** in full **Sheogorath** regalia, playfully interacting with an audio technician as he re-records lines. His growing bewilderment at having to revisit familiar dialogue is a testament to his comedic timing and deep understanding of the character. It's a joy to see **Johnson** so clearly enjoying himself, especially given the serious health battle he faced 18 months ago. His presence alone is a powerful reminder of why **Oblivion**'s voice acting remains so beloved.

## The Mad God's Return

**Wes Johnson** has been a cornerstone of the **Elder Scrolls** universe for years, lending his distinctive voice to characters across **Morrowind**, **Oblivion**, and **Skyrim**. His work as the Imperial males in **Oblivion** provided the game's ubiquitous, often stoic, voices, making his turn as the unhinged Daedric Prince of Madness all the more impactful. **Johnson** began his career in acting and comedy, honing his skills in stand-up, improvisation, and sketch comedy before making a significant mark in radio, TV, film, and video games. His return as **Sheogorath** for this promotional material is a welcome nod to the game's legacy and a clear indication of the affection developers and fans alike hold for his performances. He has also recently appeared in **Bethesda**'s latest title, **Starfield**, further cementing his status as a key voice in the studio's pantheon.

## Community Echoes and Lingering Concerns

The online reaction to the video has been overwhelmingly positive, with many fans expressing their delight at seeing **Wes Johnson** back in such a vibrant role. The comments sections are filled with praise for his performance and well wishes for his continued health. However, beneath the surface of appreciation, a familiar undercurrent of discontent persists among PC players. Despite the celebratory nature of the video, many players continue to report significant technical issues with **Oblivion Remastered** on PC. Performance hitches and a wide array of bugs, some of which echo problems from the original release, continue to mar the experience for a portion of the player base. This juxtaposition of joyful promotional content and ongoing technical woes highlights a common tension in the gaming community when beloved older titles are revisited.

## What's Next

The **Oblivion Remastered** version for Nintendo Switch 2 is slated for release in August. While this promotional video celebrates the game's enduring charm and the talent of its voice cast, players on PC are hoping for patches that address the reported technical shortcomings.

tr.title: Sheogorath Geri Döndü: Wes Johnson Oblivion Remastered Tanıtım Videosunda
tr.summary: Oblivion Remastered'ın Nintendo Switch 2 sürümü için yayınlanan yeni tanıtım videosunda Wes Johnson, Sheogorath karakterine geri dönüyor. Hayranlar Johnson'ın geri dönüşünden memnun ancak teknik sorunlar devam ediyor.
tr.body:
Deliliğin Prensi Sheogorath geri döndü ve bu kez **Oblivion Remastered**'ın Nintendo Switch 2 sürümü için bir tanıtım videosunda kendi tarzındaki kaosu getirdi. **Elder Scrolls** evrenindeki birçok unutulmaz karakterin seslendirmesini yapan veteren seslendirme sanatçısı **Wes Johnson**, Sheogorath karakterine geri dönüyor. Sonuç, standart oyun fragmanlarının çok ötesinde, eğlenceli ve samimi bir video oldu.

 ## Deliliğin Tanrısının Dönüşü
 **Wes Johnson**, **Elder Scrolls** evreninde yıllardır önemli bir figür olarak yer alıyor. **Morrowind**, **Oblivion** ve **Skyrim** gibi oyunlarda çeşitli karakterlere ses verdi. **Oblivion**'daki İmparatorluk erkek karakterlerinin seslendirmesini yaparak oyunun her yerinde bulunan, genellikle ciddi olan seslere hayat verdi. Sheogorath olarak yaptığı çalışma ise onun komik zamanlamasını ve karakteri anlamasını gösteriyor. Sağlık sorunlarıyla mücadele ettiği 18 ay sonra böyle bir projede yer alması, **Oblivion**'un seslendirmesinin neden bu kadar sevilendiğini hatırlatıyor.

 ## Topluluk Tepkileri ve Süregelen Endişeler
 Videonun yayınlanmasıyla birlikte hayranların tepkileri çok olumlu oldu. Manyalar **Wes Johnson**'ın performansını övdü ve sağlığına dileklerde bulundu. Ancak PC oyuncuları arasında teknik sorunların devam ettiği görülüyor. **Oblivion Remastered**'da performans sorunları ve çeşitli hatalar, bazı oyuncuların deneyimini olumsuz etkiliyor. Bu durum, sevgili eski oyunların güncellenmesi sırasında ortaya çıkan sıkıntıları gösteriyor.

 ## Sonraki Adımlar
 **Oblivion Remastered**'ın Nintendo Switch 2 sürümü Ağustos ayında çıkacak. Bu tanıtım videosu, oyunun kalıcı çekiciliğini ve seslendirme kadrosunun yeteneğini vurguluyor. PC oyuncuları ise teknik sorunların giderilmesini bekliyor.

es.title: El regreso de Wes Johnson como Sheogorath para la promoción de Oblivion Remastered
es.summary: Un nuevo video promocional para la versión de Nintendo Switch 2 de Oblivion Remastered presenta al veterano actor de voz Wes Johnson repitiendo su icónico papel como Sheogorath. Los fanáticos están emocionados de ver a Johnson de vuelta en acción, aunque algunos problemas técnicos persisten.
es.body:
El excéntrico Príncipe de la Locura ha regresado, y esta vez trae su marca de caos delicioso a un video promocional para la próxima versión de Nintendo Switch 2 de **Oblivion Remastered**. El veterano actor de voz de **Elder Scrolls**, **Wes Johnson**, el hombre detrás de innumerables personajes memorables, incluyendo los varones imperiales por defecto en Oblivion y, por supuesto, el inigualable **Sheogorath**, ha regresado al estudio de grabación. El resultado es una encantadora visión detrás de escena que es mucho más entretenida que el típico tráiler de juego.

 
   El video captura a **Johnson** en pleno atuendo de **Sheogorath**, interactuando juguetonamente con un técnico de audio mientras vuelve a grabar líneas. Su creciente perplejidad al tener que revisitar diálogos familiares es un testimonio de su timing cómico y profunda comprensión del personaje. Es un placer ver a **Johnson** disfrutando claramente de sí mismo, especialmente considerando la seria batalla de salud que enfrentó hace 18 meses. Su presencia sola es un poderoso recordatorio de por qué la actuación de voz de **Oblivion** sigue siendo tan querida.

 
   ## El regreso del Dios Loco
 
   **Wes Johnson** ha sido una columna vertebral del universo de **Elder Scrolls** durante años, prestando su voz distintiva a personajes en **Morrowind**, **Oblivion** y **Skyrim**. Su trabajo como varones imperiales en **Oblivion** proporcionó las voces ubicuas y a menudo estoicas del juego, lo que hizo que su interpretación del desquiciado Príncipe Daédrico de la Locura fuera aún más impactante. **Johnson** comenzó su carrera en actuación y comedia, perfeccionando sus habilidades en stand-up, improvisación y comedia de sketch antes de dejar una huella significativa en la radio, la TV, el cine y los videojuegos. Su regreso como **Sheogorath** para este material promocional es un gesto de bienvenida hacia el legado del juego y una clara indicación del cariño que desarrolladores y fanáticos por igual sienten por sus actuaciones.

 
   ## Ecos de la comunidad y preocupaciones persistentes
 
   La reacción en línea al video ha sido abrumadoramente positiva, con muchos fanáticos expresando su deleite al ver a **Wes Johnson** de vuelta en un papel tan vibrante. Las secciones de comentarios están llenas de elogios para su actuación y deseos de buena salud. Sin embargo, bajo la superficie de aprecio, una corriente subyacente de descontento persiste entre los jugadores de PC. A pesar de la naturaleza celebratoria del video, muchos jugadores siguen informando problemas técnicos significativos con **Oblivion Remastered** en PC. Los problemas de rendimiento y una amplia gama de errores, algunos de los cuales ecoan problemas de la versión original, siguen empañando la experiencia para una parte de la base de jugadores. Esta yuxtaposición de contenido promocional alegre y problemas técnicos en curso resalta una tensión común en la comunidad de juegos cuando títulos antiguos queridos son revisitados.

 
   ## Próximos pasos
 
   La versión de **Oblivion Remastered** para Nintendo Switch 2 está programada para su lanzamiento en agosto. Mientras que este video promocional celebra el encanto duradero del juego y el talento de su elenco de voces, los jugadores en PC esperan parches que aborden las deficiencias técnicas informadas.

content_raw: Oblivion Remastered releases on Nintendo Switch 2 in August, which normally would be wholly irrelevant to PC Gamer. We've been merrily exploring revamped Cyrodiil for well over a year at this point. But you might want to hide your stealth archer in the corner of whatever dungeon you're exploring and check out Bethesda's latest promotional video for the Switch 2 launch. It's a little different from the usual fare of game footage and dramatic voiceovers. To herald the Switch 2 version's imminent release, Bethesda brought back veteran Elder Scrolls voice actor Wes Johnson—who plays many characters across the series including Oblivion's default Imperial males—to reprise his most colourful role in the series, the mad, cheese-loving god Sheogorath. In the video, Johnson—dressed as and in the role of Sheogorath—records lines in a sound booth and causes general mischief with the aid of an exasperated audio technician. As the video progresses, the Prince of Madness becomes increasingly baffled as to why he has to record lines he's already done before. It's a shameless bit of marketing fluff, but it's nonetheless entertaining to see Johnson in full swing as Sheogorath. It's also a relief that he has apparently made a full recovery from the life-threatening medical emergency he suffered 18 months ago, during which he was hospitalised and put into an induced coma. The responses to the video are similarly pleased to see Johnson in action. But there is an undercurrent of discontent to many of the comments. These mainly centre around the remaster's widely reported technical issues on PC. Not only do many Steam reviews report performance hitches while exploring Cyrodiil, but the game also suffers from a wide array of bugs . Some of these have been around since the original Oblivion released in 2006, while others are entirely new. What doesn't help is that Bethesda and Virtuos appear to have abandoned the PC version. While Oblivion Remastered received a couple of patches after launch, the last one—update 1.2—arrived over a year ago. Consequently, recent Steam reviews have dropped down to Mixed, though the game still has a Mostly Positive rating overall. Let's hope the Switch 2 launch brings a bit of PC TLC too.
